STEP 1 - Scene: This shows a single whole fruit, likely a mango or nectarine-like peach with reddish-orange skin, resting on a white plate. Photo is taken from a low, oblique angle looking up, so the plate appears distorted. Not a full meal, just one fruit.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White rectangular/rounded dish, roughly 25 cm long along its longest undistorted edge; treat as a dinner-plate-sized vessel, diameter ~24 cm, area ≈ 3.14 x 12^2 ≈ 452 cm^2. The fruit is roughly 9 cm long by 7.5 cm wide, so it is about the size of a medium mango.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole fruit (mango/peach-type), skin intact.

STEP 4 - Area: Fruit footprint about 9 x 7.5 cm, roughly 50 cm^2, about 11% of the plate area. Only this item is food.

STEP 5 - Volume: The whole fruit is about 3/4 of its length in height on the plate, so envelope ≈ 50 cm^2 x 6.5 cm ≈ 325 ml. For a whole fruit, the actual volume is closer to an ellipsoid: (4/3)π(4.5 x 3.75 x 3.75) ≈ 265 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit density is about 0.9-1.0 g/ml (dense, not loose pieces). Using 265 ml x 0.95 ≈ 250 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Mango/peach-type raw fruit ≈ 60 kcal per 100 g. 250 g x 0.60 ≈ 150 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium mango or large peach weighs roughly 200-300 g and ~120-180 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
